### `firehose/`

The persistent event pipeline behind `com.atproto.sync.subscribeRepos`: a durable monotonic
sequencer (`repo_seq`, V028) plus a Tokio broadcast fan-out, shared as `AppState.firehose`.
Three files — `mod.rs` (sequencer, bare `emit_*` primitives, and the staged-transaction path
`lock_emit`/`EmitGuard`/`Pending*`), `events.rs` (wire-facing event model + DAG-CBOR stored
encoding), `replay.rs` (cursor replay over the durable log) — with every public type
re-exported at `crate::firehose::*`. The invariants that make it subtle (persist-before-
broadcast under one `emit_lock`, the lock-before-transaction deadlock rule on this crate's
single-connection pool, staging into a caller's transaction, cancellation recovery via
`insert_at_frontier`, and the emission map of which routes emit which frames) are documented
in `firehose/mod.rs`'s module and item docs — read those before touching any emit path.

### `crawler.rs`

Outbound `com.atproto.sync.requestCrawl` notifier (`AppState.crawlers`). Fires on startup and on
**every** firehose broadcast frame — lifecycle frames included, so a relay that silently dropped
its subscription is re-invited even when the only news is a post-migration `#account`/`#sync`.
Fire-and-forget, rate-limited to one notification per crawler per 30s, retried with backoff;
configured via `[crawlers] urls` / `EZPDS_CRAWLERS` (default `["https://bsky.network"]`, empty
disables). Mechanism and invariants: the module doc in `src/crawler.rs`.

### `relay_status.rs`

The inbound half of federation health: a `com.atproto.sync.getHostStatus` client asking the
upstream relay what it knows about this PDS, backing `GET /v1/admin/relay-status` (which compares
the relay's cursor against our exact sequencer head — see that route's row below, and
`admin_request_crawl.rs` for the companion action). Total, never fatal: every failure becomes a
`RelayReport` variant, so the readout always renders the outcome — what the relay said, or that
it could not be asked. Details: the module doc in `src/relay_status.rs`.

### `rate_limit.rs`

Reference-parity request rate limiting. The pure sliding-window algorithm lives in
`auth/rate_limit.rs` (Functional Core); this module is the Imperative Shell owning the
process-level limiters and the Axum middleware. Three families — global per-IP, per-endpoint
per-IP (guess-target endpoint pairs share one limiter instance so alternating endpoints can't
double a guess budget), and per-account write points charged in `record_write::commit_repo_write`
on the **authenticated** DID — all off when `[rate_limit] enabled = false`, all tunable via
`[rate_limit]` / `EZPDS_RATE_LIMIT_*` (a knob of `0` disables that limiter). The family
rosters, exemptions, and `RateLimit-*` header behavior: the module doc.

## Metrics

`GET /metrics` serves the federation-health instrument set. `metrics::names` in
`src/metrics.rs` is the single source of truth: each constant documents what it measures and
who records it, a unit test pins the rendered Prometheus names (counters gain their `_total`
suffix at export), and label values never come from request data. `GET /v1/admin/health`
mirrors the sweeps' last-run state as JSON via `sweep_status.rs`, so operators keep the
signal with `[telemetry] metrics_enabled` off.

## Hard Rules

**Routes must not import from other routes.**
If two routes share logic, that logic belongs in `auth/` (pure) or `db/` (queries). A route
importing from another route creates hidden coupling and makes it impossible to reason about
a handler in isolation.

**Every `.rs` file with runtime behavior must have a pattern comment.**
Add `// pattern: Functional Core`, `// pattern: Imperative Shell`, or
`// pattern: Mixed (unavoidable)` at the top of any file containing functions or
orchestration logic. Files with only types, constants, or re-exports are exempt.

**`db/` submodules own queries, not transactions.**
Business-logic transactions (multi-table atomic operations) live in the route handler or
a dedicated helper called by the handler — not inside `db/` functions. `db/` functions
accept `&SqlitePool` or `&mut SqliteTransaction`; they never open transactions themselves
unless the operation is inherently single-table.

**Authentication must never be cookie-based; permissive CORS on the public surface depends on it.**
`app.rs` applies `CorsLayer::permissive()` to the public surface (landing, `.well-known`, OAuth,
agent registration, all XRPC, static assets) but deliberately **not** to the admin/provisioning
`/v1/*` surface (same-origin only). Permissive CORS is safe only because every auth path is
Bearer/DPoP/signed-request — never an ambient cookie — so a hostile origin cannot ride a logged-in
user's credentials. If any future auth mechanism becomes cookie-based, the permissive CORS layer
must be tightened (explicit origin allowlist + credentials handling) in the same change.

## Adding a New Route

1. Create `src/routes/<name>.rs` with `// pattern: Imperative Shell` at the top.
2. If the handler needs shared auth logic → add to `auth/` (pure) or use an existing extractor.
3. If the handler needs a new DB query → add to the appropriate `db/` submodule.
4. If it's an XRPC procedure: a JSON input body is parsed with `LexiconInput<T>` (never bare
   `axum::Json<T>`) after vendoring its lexicon document (`crates/pds/lexicons/README.md`); a
   no-input procedure takes `NoInputBody` instead. Both must be the handler's final extractor.
5. Register in `src/app.rs` router.
6. Add a `.bru` file in `bruno/` (see root AGENTS.md).

## Adding a New DB Query

1. Identify the owning entity (`accounts`, `oauth`, etc.).
2. Add the function to the matching `db/<entity>.rs` file.
3. If no matching file exists, create one with `// pattern: Imperative Shell`.
4. Export the function and any new data struct via `db/mod.rs` (`pub mod <entity>;`).

content.subject: Fix 1: flat atproto error shape on /xrpc surface + wallet tolerant parser
content.description: Middleware flattens ApiError responses on /xrpc/* to {"error":"PascalName","message":...} with canonical XRPC names (ExpiredToken, InvalidToken, AuthMissing, AuthenticationRequired, RateLimitExceeded, InternalServerError...). Provisioning /v1/* keeps nested envelope. Wallet Rust parser becomes shape-tolerant. Update tests.

content.subject: Fix 2: token lifetimes + refresh grace/reuse detection
content.description: Access token 300s → 15 min; refresh TTL 24h → 2 weeks (rolling); add concurrent-refresh grace window (old refresh token remains exchangeable briefly for the same DPoP key / returns same result) and reuse detection.
content.activeForm: Extending token lifetimes and refresh semantics

content.subject: Fix 3: normalize rpc: scope aud matching across proxy and getServiceAuth
content.description: xrpc_dispatch passes raw atproto-proxy header (with #fragment) to require_rpc; getServiceAuth strips fragment. Normalize: match on DID, treat fragment as optional refinement, accept scopes written either way.

content.subject: Fix 4: implement private_key_jwt client auth + validate client metadata
content.description: Accept client_assertion (RFC 7523, ES256, 30s clock tolerance) at token/revoke endpoints; fetch client jwks/jwks_uri; enforce token_endpoint_auth_method from client metadata; validate grant_types/response_types/scope/dpop_bound_access_tokens.

content.subject: Fix 5: bind dpop_jkt at PAR/code issuance; make state optional
content.description: Store dpop_jkt from PAR DPoP proof (when present) on the pending authorization + auth code rows; enforce at token exchange. Drop the nonstandard mandatory state at PAR.

# Database Module

Last verified: 2026-07-29

## Latest Updates

- **V060**: Adds nullable `match_code` + `push_dispatched_at` TEXT to `pending_oauth_authorizations` — the push-to-approve (Phase C) columns for wallet-confirmed OAuth consent. Derived-status doctrine: both NULL = no `login-approval` push was dispatched and approval needs no number (exactly the pre-V060 behavior for every request). Written once, together, by `set_push_dispatched` — a guarded single-use UPDATE (`status='pending' AND match_code IS NULL`) so a second dispatch can never rotate the number the page already displays and a resolved request can never have the requirement retrofitted. The approve route then refuses an approval whose `matchCode` doesn't equal the stored code (403, request left pending — checked server-side, after signature/authority verification, outside the signed envelope); denials never require it. The dispatch trigger lives in `routes/oauth_authorize.rs::dispatch_login_approval_push` (login_hint resolved to a local active account with **local lookups only**), and the audit trail gains the `push_dispatched` event (`detail: {devices, pushed_to}`). Query functions in `pending_oauth_authorizations.rs`.

- **V058**: Adds the Custos side of the blind-courier notification relay — three tables. `notification_sender_keys` holds the instance's versioned HPKE sender secrets (`kid` INTEGER PK AUTOINCREMENT — the version devices see in each envelope, never reused; `secret_key_encrypted` AES-256-GCM-wrapped under the master KEK exactly like `iroh_identity` V022, and registered as `SecretFamily::NotificationSenderKeys` in `kek.rs` so `pds rewrap-master-key` covers it — the one family with an INTEGER key, cast to TEXT in the inventory's SELECT). Status is derived from timestamps (the `claim_codes` doctrine): both NULL = **active** (published, and the newest one seals); `retired_at` set = **retired** (still published so a payload sealed just before a rotation still verifies, never seals again); `revoked_at` set = **revoked** (out of the published set immediately — the compromise path), the row surviving as a tombstone so its `kid` is never reissued. `notification_registrations` is keyed **(did, device_uuid)** and deliberately does **not** FK to `devices`: those rows are deleted inside the DID-promotion transaction (`routes/create_did.rs`) and the table FKs to `pending_accounts`, so a registration anchored there would die exactly when the account starts mattering; `device_uuid` is app-generated and stable, registration happens post-promotion over the `authenticate_access` seam, and `push_handle` stays NULL until the relay round trip succeeds (so a relay that is down at registration time loses a handle, not a device key). `admin_notification_registrations` is the operator analog keyed by `admin_devices.id` — an operator device authenticates as a device, not an account. `purge_account` deletes the account-keyed rows (the schema-walking FK test enforces this); the admin rows are cleaned on device revoke. Query functions in `notifications.rs`.

- **V057**: Adds `waitlist_signups`, the public interest-signup store behind the `waitlist` capability (`[waitlist] enabled`, off by default): `email` PK (stored normalized via `uniqueness::normalize_email`, so a repeat signup is an idempotent unique-violation no-op rather than a duplicate row or an enumeration oracle), nullable `handle` (optional self-reported atproto handle — syntactically validated by `identity::handle::validate_handle_structure`, deliberately never resolved: it is interest signal, not an authenticated identity claim), `created_at`. **Deliberately no foreign keys**: signups predate any account, so the table stays off the account-purge path entirely (the schema-walking purge test never sees it). Rowid-cursor pagination (V052 doctrine) backs the operator readout. Query functions in `waitlist.rs`; routes in `routes/waitlist_signup.rs` (`POST /waitlist`, public + CORS'd, gated on `[waitlist] enabled`) and `routes/admin_waitlist.rs` (`GET /v1/admin/waitlist`, available regardless of the switch — it reads data already collected).

- **V056**: Adds `pending_oauth_authorizations` + `oauth_consent_audit_events`, the wallet-confirmed OAuth consent primitive (unblocks the sovereign/passwordless lockout where `oauth_authorize.rs` maps a NULL `password_hash` to `WrongPassword`). `pending_oauth_authorizations` is the single-use request the consent page creates in place of the password check: `request_id` PK (high-entropy), unique `user_code` (the distinctly-formatted `XXXX-XXXX` login code from `code_gen::generate_login_code`), a client-metadata snapshot (`client_id` FK→`oauth_clients`, `client_name`) + the full authorization context (redirect_uri, code_challenge[_method], state, response_type, requested_scope), requesting `origin`/`ip`/`user_agent`, optional `login_hint` DID, `status` (CHECK `pending`/`approved`/`denied`/`expired`/`completed`), the bound `account_did` + `granted_scope` set on approval, and `created_at`/`expires_at` (~5-min TTL). **Derived-status doctrine:** `expired` is computed from `expires_at` at read time, not persisted — no background sweep; lapsed rows are reclaimed opportunistically on the next creation (`cleanup_expired_pending_authorizations`, the `oauth_par_requests`/`transfers` precedent). Terminal transitions are guarded single-statement UPDATEs (`approve`/`deny`/`complete`), so a replayed device-key approval envelope lands on an already-terminal row and wins nothing — the envelope's `request_id` binding + this single-use row together subsume a nonce store. `account_did` is deliberately **not** an `accounts` FK (ephemeral row, DID already verified against authoritative PLC at approval; keeps the table off the account-purge path, like `agent_child_deletions.child_did`). `oauth_consent_audit_events` is append-only in the `agent_audit_events` (V040) / `admin_audit_events` (V052) mold (INSERT+SELECT only, rowid-cursor, **no FKs** so the trail outlives its ephemeral row + subject): `request_created`/`approved`/`denied`/`completed`, `detail` mechanical facts only. Query functions in `pending_oauth_authorizations.rs`; routes in `routes/oauth_consent.rs` (`GET /oauth/authorize/consent-request` wallet preview, `GET /oauth/authorize/status` slow_down-throttled poll, `POST /oauth/authorize/approve` device-key-signed, `POST /oauth/authorize/complete` code issuance) plus the wallet path added to `routes/oauth_authorize.rs`'s `get_authorization`.

- **V055**: Drops `pending_accounts.pending_share_{1,2,3}` — the retired server-side DID ceremony's idempotent share store. V011 added these so the pre-inversion `POST /v1/dids` path could return the same three Shamir shares across retries (avoiding an orphaned Share 2 in `accounts.recovery_share`). The ceremony inversion moved share generation client-side, and this migration retires the legacy server-side path entirely: a did:plc request now *requires* the wallet's `recoveryKey` + `escrowShare` (400 otherwise), the server never generates or splits a secret, and did:web promotes with no escrow. Nothing reads or writes these columns anymore — they only ever put two-of-three reconstruction material into Litestream backups. Forward-only `DROP COLUMN` (SQLite ≥ 3.35): plain nullable TEXT, no index/FK/default, so it applies cleanly on a populated `pending_accounts`. `pending_did` (V008) and `pending_plc_registered_at` (V054) stay — they gate the share-independent DID-pre-store / plc.directory re-POST retry logic. `accounts.recovery_share` (V010) is untouched (dropped later by the old-account re-key migration).

- **V054**: Adds nullable `pending_plc_registered_at` TEXT to `pending_accounts` — the confirmed-PLC-registration marker the DID ceremony (`routes/create_did.rs`, `POST /v1/dids`) reads on a retry. `pending_did` (V008) was overloaded as proof of a completed plc.directory registration, but it is pre-stored *before* the `post_to_plc_directory` POST, so a retry after a **failed** POST saw it set, took the skip-plc branch, and promoted a DID that may never have registered globally (an "active" account whose DID doesn't resolve on the network — handle resolution/federation/PLC-monitoring silently fail later). This column is stamped (`mark_plc_registered`, `datetime('now')`) only *after* a 2xx from plc.directory; the retry branch (`pre_store_did` for the client-share path, `pre_store_did_and_shares` for the legacy path) skips the POST only when it is set and otherwise re-POSTs the idempotent signed genesis op (same op → same DID). Share reuse stays gated on `pending_did` as before — the two decisions are orthogonal (shares stay stable while the POST retries). Stamped before the promotion transaction, so a retry whose promotion failed still skips the (already-done) POST; dropped with the `pending_accounts` row at promotion, like `pending_did`. Derived-status doctrine (NULL = not yet confirmed). No writer/reader outside `create_did.rs`.

- **V053**: Adds `recovery_otps`, the email-OTP store gating the escrow-assisted recovery *release* flow. Same SHA-256-hashed, 1-hour, single-use envelope as `password_reset_tokens` (V014) / `plc_operation_tokens` (V033) / `account_deletion_tokens` (V034) / `email_tokens` (V036): `token_hash` PK, `did` FK→`accounts`, `expires_at`, nullable `used_at`, `created_at`, plus `idx_recovery_otps_did`. `POST /v1/recovery/initiate` mints one (always-200, no enumeration — the `requestPasswordReset` posture) and the opening `POST /v1/recovery/release` call consumes it (atomic single-use, bound to `(token_hash, did)` so it can neither be replayed nor spent against another account). A dedicated table (not a new `purpose` on an existing one) keeps the recovery credential from ever being redeemable in another flow. Query functions in `recovery_otps.rs`; `account_delete::purge_account` deletes these rows. The release *state machine* rides V050's existing `recovery_escrow.release_requested_at`/`release_pending_until` columns (written now, for the first time, by the release flow) and appends `release_requested`/`release_cancelled`/`released` rows to `recovery_audit_events` (the vocabulary V050's CHECK already reserved).

- **V052**: Adds `admin_audit_events`, the **server-wide** append-only admin action audit log — the unified answer to "what have admins done on this relay?". One row per privileged mutating admin action: `actor` (the `AdminActor` log string — `master-token` / `device:<id>`, plus `pairing-code` for device enrollments, whose acting credential is the consumed code, not an existing admin identity), `action` (typed vocabulary in `admin_audit.rs::AdminAuditAction` — takedown/restore, credential sweep, claim-code mint/revoke, pairing-code mint, device register/revoke, transfer cancel, request-crawl, email repair, reset-token issuance, signing-key creation), nullable `subject` (account DID / device id / transfer id / claim code), `outcome`, and a `detail` JSON of mechanical facts (counts, resulting status — never codes or token material). **Deliberately no foreign keys**: the trail must outlive its subjects (a takedown row survives the account's permanent deletion; `purge_account` touches nothing here), unlike the account-scoped `operator_account_audit_events` (V046), which the repair routes now double-write alongside. Only real state transitions are recorded — idempotent repeats (re-revoking a revoked device) write nothing. Writes join the mutating route's transaction where one exists; everywhere a failed audit write fails the request (fail closed — a privileged action must not land unattributed). Rowid-cursor pagination (V040 doctrine) plus `action`/`actor`/`subject` equality indexes back `GET /v1/admin/audit` (`routes/admin_audit.rs`) and the Brass Console's Audit screen. Queries in `admin_audit.rs`.

- **V051**: Adds `account_labels` (WITHOUT ROWID, PK `(did, labeler_did, val)`, FK→`accounts(did)`, `idx_account_labels_labeler`), the watched-labeler flag store behind the operator triage view: one row per account-level label *currently in force* from a `[labeler] watched` labeler, reconciled each `labeler_watch.rs` pass (a negated/expired label's row is deleted, not tombstoned — the table is an explicitly rebuildable cache of external labeler state, unlike the derived-status doctrine tables). `cts` is the labeler's creation timestamp (shown to the operator); `first_seen_at` records first local observation — the seam a future push-notifier uses to tell a genuinely new flag from backfill. Query functions in `account_labels.rs`; the listing-side predicates (`FLAGGED_SQL` flagged-first ordering + composite cursor, `count_accounts_admin_flagged`) live in `accounts.rs`. `account_delete::purge_account` deletes these account-owned rows before `accounts` (no FK cascade, as ever).

- **V050**: Adds the escrow storage for the one Shamir share Custos holds under the client-generated share model: `recovery_escrow` (WITHOUT ROWID, `did` PK FK→`accounts`; `share_encrypted` is the 42-byte v2 share envelope AES-256-GCM-wrapped under the master KEK from day one — registered as `SecretFamily::RecoveryEscrow` in `kek.rs`, so `pds rewrap-master-key` covers it via the generic-length `crypto::{encrypt,decrypt}_secret_bytes` pair; `rotated_at` NULL = never replaced, `release_requested_at`/`release_pending_until` NULL = no release in flight — derived-status doctrine, written only by the escrow release flow) and `recovery_audit_events` (append-only, the `agent_audit_events` V040 doctrine: INSERT/SELECT only, rowid cursors, `purge_account` the sole remover; a CHECK constraint reserves the full event vocabulary — `deposited`/`rotated`/`deleted` written by the owner endpoints, `release_requested`/`release_cancelled`/`released` reserved for the release flow; `detail` carries mechanical facts only, never share material). Query functions in `recovery_escrow.rs` and `recovery_audit.rs`; wired by `routes/recovery_escrow.rs` (`PUT`/`DELETE /v1/recovery/escrow-share`) and by `routes/create_did.rs`' client-share ceremony path (the genesis-time deposit + `deposited` audit event land inside the promotion transaction). The legacy `accounts.recovery_share` column (V010) is deliberately untouched — it is dropped by the old-account re-key migration once existing accounts move to the new model.
- **V049**: Adds `agent_child_deletions`, the durable tombstone for a parent's deletion of a sovereign child agent. Deleting a child reuses the deactivate + `delete_after` + reaper pipeline, so the reaper eventually calls `account_delete::purge_account`, which drops the child's account, repo, handle, blobs, `agent_identities` row *and* its whole `agent_audit_events` trail — the child's own history cannot outlive it. This table is the V030-style anchor for "the deletion is auditable after the fact": keyed by `child_did` with **no FK to `accounts` on that column** so a child purge leaves it intact, but with `parent_did REFERENCES accounts(did)` so the parent's audit view outlives the child. `purge_account` deletes it `WHERE parent_did = ?` (reclaimed when the *parent* is deleted), **never** `WHERE child_did = ?`. `handle`/`registration_id` are denormalized because their source rows are purged with the child. Queries in `agent_child_deletions.rs`.
- **V047**: Rebuilds `agent_identities` for sovereign child agents (nullable-`parent_did` + `child` registration type, plus the new `agent_child_provisionings` table). **Rebuild invariant, learned the hard way (v0.5.1's production deploy failed on this):** dropping the old parent implicit-deletes its rows while child FKs still reference the table name, so *every* table with an FK into `agent_identities (id)` must be cycled through a temp stash around the swap — `agent_claim_attempts` (V037) *and* `agent_audit_events` (V040). The audit stash carries rowids explicitly (`CREATE TABLE AS SELECT` drops them; the audit trail's pagination cursors are rowid-based). A fresh-DB migration run can't catch a missed child (the tables are empty), so any future parent-table rebuild needs a populated-upgrade-path test like `v047_rebuild_preserves_audit_events_and_claim_attempts` / `v038_rebuild_preserves_child_rows_and_allows_null_did` in `mod.rs`.

- **V046**: Adds `operator_account_audit_events`, the durable audit trail for admin account repair. `email_updated` records the authenticated admin actor plus previous/new normalized addresses; `reset_token_issued` records issuance without token material (refused with 400 for a passwordless account, so no token or audit row is written — a key-sovereign account is recovered through its escrowed key share, not a password reset). Both writes are atomic with their repair operation, and permanent account deletion removes these account-owned rows before deleting `accounts`.

- **V045**: Normalizes existing `accounts.email` / `pending_accounts.email` rows to lowercase (trimmed) in place — a data-only migration, no schema change. Both columns already carry a UNIQUE index (`idx_accounts_email` / `idx_pending_accounts_email`), so the normalizing `UPDATE` fails loudly (aborting the whole migration transaction) if two rows would collide once normalized, rather than silently merging them; an operator must resolve the collision manually before the migration can apply. Pairs with the normalize-on-every-read/write-path fix in `uniqueness.rs` (`normalize_email`, shared by `email_taken`) and `accounts.rs` (`resolve_by_email`, `update_account_email`) — the reference PDS lowercases emails on store and lookup, and without this the account-creation routes' byte-exact matching let a differently-cased signup email silently fail later matches (e.g. `requestPasswordReset` 200-and-no-op with no way to discover the mismatch).
- **V044**: Adds nullable `did_web_hosting_enabled_at` TEXT to `accounts` — the opt-in flag for Custos-managed did:web hosting. Derived-status doctrine (V008/V026/V004): NULL = hosting off (never enabled or turned back off); a timestamp = when it was last enabled. The `.well-known/did.json` serve route (`routes/did_json.rs`) reads through this column joined to `did_documents` and the active-lifecycle gate (`dids::serve_hosted_did_document`), so an account that isn't opted in 404s exactly like an unknown host — no opt-in existence oracle. did:plc accounts never set it (their document lives on plc.directory). Writers/readers in `dids.rs`: `set_did_web_hosting` (toggle), `did_web_hosting_enabled` (probe), `serve_hosted_did_document` (gated serve). The opt-in toggle + the authenticated non-PLC document-edit path (direct `did_documents` overwrite via `rewrite_did_document` + `#identity` firehose frame) live in `routes/did_web_hosting.rs`.
- **V043**: Adds `sovereign_session_nonces`, a dedicated DID-scoped anti-replay store for sovereign-session signed requests. Its `(did, nonce)` primary key makes insert-if-absent atomic and permits the same random nonce across different identities; the DID FK binds rows to hosted accounts, and `idx_sovereign_session_nonces_seen_at` supports bounded stale-row cleanup. The query layer rejects a retention threshold at or below the full `2 * SOVEREIGN_TIMESTAMP_WINDOW_SECS` replay-acceptance span, so sweeping cannot reopen a replay while its signed timestamp is still acceptable. It deliberately does not reuse `admin_nonces`, whose rows are owned by admin device ids. It **is** shared by every wallet-signed account proof, not only sovereign sessions: `deleteAccount`'s deletion proof spends its nonce here too. The domain-versioned envelopes make a nonce non-transferable between surfaces anyway, so sharing only strengthens the property (one nonce, one proof, per DID) and keeps these rows on the account-purge path already covered by the schema-walking test rather than adding a table to remember.
- **V042**: Seeds the identity wallet's **canonical** OAuth client row: client_id `https://identitywallet.obsign.org/oauth/client-metadata.json` with redirect URI `org.obsign.identitywallet:/oauth/callback` — the reverse-FQDN scheme⇄host pairing the atproto OAuth spec requires for a native client's private-use redirect (and third-party AS's like bsky.social enforce; the PAR handler now enforces it too for discoverable clients). The wallet's OAuth identity is this fixed URL (it no longer varies with the configured Custos); seeding the row lets any instance accept the wallet without an outbound fetch of the canonical document. Uses `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` (corrects a previously cached copy). The V013 row is deliberately kept so pre-transition wallet builds (old client_id + old scheme) keep working. The client-metadata route (`routes/oauth_client_metadata.rs`) serves the same canonical document, with a loopback-`public_url` exception for local dev.
- **Operator transfer visibility/cancel** (no new migration — extends V027/V029/V030 semantics): `transfers.status` gains a new **terminal** value, `cancelled` (operator interruption). No schema change is needed: the column is unconstrained TEXT, and both partial UNIQUE indexes (`idx_transfers_active_did`/`idx_transfers_active_code`) enumerate the *active* statuses, so a cancelled row frees the per-DID and per-code slots exactly like `complete`/`expired`, and every accept/complete lookup (which filters on the active list) ignores it. `transfers.rs` gains `list_inflight_transfers` (the operator view: `accepted`/`completing` rows regardless of expiry — completion has no expiry predicate, so a lapsed accepted transfer can still finish — plus unexpired `pending`; `(created_at, id)` keyset pages; deliberately never selects `code`, a live account-takeover credential), `mark_transfer_cancelled` (UPDATE guarded on the active statuses), and `revoke_transfer_device` (single-credential `revoked_at` tombstone, V030 doctrine). The cross-table cancel transaction (sweep-if-lapsed → cancel → tombstone accepted credential → `transfer.cancelled` audit event) lives in the root `transfer.rs::cancel_transfer`, backing `GET /v1/admin/transfers` + `POST /v1/admin/transfers/{id}/cancel` (`routes/admin_transfers.rs`).
- **V041**: Adds nullable `revoked_at` TEXT to `claim_codes` plus a composite `(created_at, code)` index — operator revocation for a minted-but-unredeemed claim code (a live signup credential). Derived-status doctrine (V004/V025): NULL = never revoked; every redemption path (the atomic single-use UPDATEs in `register_device.rs`/`create_account_xrpc.rs`/`create_mobile_account.rs` and the `claim_code_valid` preflight) additionally requires `revoked_at IS NULL`, so revocation closes redemption exactly like expiry, and the row survives as the audit record. Deliberately an in-place ALTER, not a rebuild: `pending_accounts.claim_code` (V005) FK-references `claim_codes (code)`, so a DROP/rename rebuild fails on any DB holding pending rows; the inventory therefore pages on the immutable `(created_at, code)` keyset (stable across VACUUM — this TEXT-keyed table's implicit rowid is not). `claim_codes.rs` gains `list_claim_codes` (newest-first keyset page, `is_expired` evaluated in SQL so "now" is derived once) and `revoke_claim_code` (guarded UPDATE `redeemed_at IS NULL AND revoked_at IS NULL`; a failed attempt is classified race-free into `AlreadyRevoked`/`Redeemed`/`NotFound` because those states are terminal). Backing `GET /v1/accounts/claim-codes` + `POST /v1/accounts/claim-codes/revoke` (admin companion's inventory screen).

Modeled on `transfer_audit_events` (V030): the query layer (`agent_audit.rs`) exposes INSERT and SELECT only — no UPDATE/DELETE exists or may be added; `account_delete::purge_account` is the sole remover (keyed through the identity — `registration_id IN (SELECT id FROM agent_identities WHERE did = ?)` — because NULL-did events still pin the identity row via the FK, ordered before the `agent_claim_attempts`/`agent_identities` deletes). Event vocabulary is the `AgentAuditEventType` enum (`registered`, `claim_initiated`, `claim_confirmed`, `claim_expired`, `token_exchanged`, `repo_write`, `blob_upload`, `revoked`); `detail` carries mechanical facts only (op counts, collections, mime/size, grant kind) — never record bodies, user codes, or token material. Pagination cursors on the table's rowid (append-only ⇒ rowid order = event order). Writers: registration + claim routes, the token endpoint, `record_write::commit_repo_write` (atomically with the CAS), `upload_blob`, the `/v1/agents` revoke route, and the `agent_claim_sweep` background pass.

- **V038**: Rebuilds `agent_identities` to make `did` **nullable** so the auth.md `anonymous` flow can register an ownerless identity (a `NULL` did = no owning account until a later claim ceremony binds one); the FK to `accounts(did)` still applies to non-NULL values. SQLite can't drop a column's NOT NULL in place, so the table is rebuilt. `PRAGMA foreign_keys` can't be toggled mid-transaction and `defer_foreign_keys` leaves an unbalanced deferred-violation counter across the parent drop/rename (dropping the old parent implicit-deletes its rows while `agent_claim_attempts(identity_id)` still references the table name), so the child rows are cycled through a temp stash — emptied before the parent swap and refilled after — keeping FK enforcement on with no orphan window. `agent_auth.rs`'s `NewAgentIdentity.did`/`AgentIdentityRow.did` become `Option`, and the jwt-bearer exchange (`oauth_token.rs`) compares the stored did against the assertion `sub` as an `Option` (a NULL-did anonymous identity is never `claimed`, so it never exchanges).
- **V037**: Adds the auth.md agent-registration state tables: `agent_identities` (FK→`accounts.did`, registration type, issuer/subject/email metadata, granted scopes JSON, service assertion material, optional claim token, active/claimed/revoked status) and `agent_claim_attempts` (FK→`agent_identities.id`, 6-digit user code, expiry, target email, pending/completed/expired status). Query functions live in `agent_auth.rs` and intentionally keep JWT validation/code generation in future route code.
- **V036**: Adds the `email_tokens` table (same SHA-256-hashed, 1-hour, single-use envelope as `password_reset_tokens` V014 / `plc_operation_tokens` V033 / `account_deletion_tokens` V034), with a `purpose` column (`confirm`|`update`) so one table backs both the `confirmEmail` and `updateEmail` flows without a token from one being redeemable in the other. `requestEmailConfirmation`/`requestEmailUpdate` insert a token (delivered via the outbound-email path); `confirmEmail`/`updateEmail` consume it (bound to `(token_hash, did, purpose)`, atomic single-use). Query functions live in `email_tokens.rs`; the confirmation-state writers `set_email_confirmed` (sets `email_confirmed_at`) and `update_account_email` (changes `email` + clears `email_confirmed_at`, reporting an `idx_accounts_email` UNIQUE collision as `Taken`) live in `accounts.rs`. This is the first migration to accompany a real outbound-email sender (`pds/src/email.rs`, `[email]` config) rather than the logged-token stub the earlier token tables shipped with.
- **V035**: Adds `block_owners`, the authoritative per-account ownership/revision table for globally content-addressed repo blocks. `blocks` still stores physical bytes once by CID, but its legacy `account_did` FK is removed during a table rebuild so account deletion no longer has to delete shared global bytes. Existing physical rows are marked `legacy_protected` because historic implicit shared references cannot be reconstructed in SQL. Repo writes insert/update both `blocks` and `block_owners`; account-scoped reads/stats/incremental-export/GC use `block_owners`; GC and account deletion remove ownership rows and reclaim only unowned, non-legacy physical bytes.
- **V034**: Adds the `account_deletion_tokens` table (same SHA-256-hashed, 1-hour, single-use envelope as `plc_operation_tokens` V033 / `password_reset_tokens` V014): email tokens gating `com.atproto.server.deleteAccount`. `requestAccountDelete` inserts a token (delivery stubbed → logged, pending an outbound-email path); `deleteAccount` consumes it (bound to `(token_hash, did)`, atomic single-use). Query functions live in `account_deletion_tokens.rs`. **Permanent-deletion note:** **no account-keyed FK cascades** — the only `ON DELETE CASCADE` in the schema hangs content-addressed ownership rows off their physical tables (`block_owners.cid`→`blocks`, `blob_owners.cid`→`blobs` since V039), never off `accounts` — so account deletion (`account_delete::purge_account`, shared by `deleteAccount` and the `deleteAfter` reaper) must delete every child row explicitly in FK order, never relying on cascade behavior (`refresh_tokens`→`sessions`; `transfer_audit_events`→`transfers`→`transfer_devices`; then the rest), reclaims on-disk blob files no other account owns (per `blob_owners`, V039), and emits an `#account` (`active=false`, `status="deleted"`) frame — but deliberately leaves `repo_seq` untouched (punching per-DID holes would break cursor-replay density), removes repo block ownership rows without deleting shared global block bytes, and does **not** tombstone the did:plc identity (the PDS holds no rotation key; ADR-0001).
- **V033**: Adds the `plc_operation_tokens` table (same SHA-256-hashed, 1-hour, single-use envelope as `password_reset_tokens` V014): email tokens that authorize `com.atproto.identity.signPlcOperation` on the interop account-migration path (ADR-0002). `requestPlcOperationSignature` inserts a token (delivery stubbed → logged, pending an outbound-email path); `signPlcOperation` consumes it. Only the plaintext's hash is stored; `consume_plc_operation_token` marks it used in one statement bound to `(token_hash, did)` so it can neither be replayed nor spent by another account. Query functions live in `plc_operation_tokens.rs`.
- **V032**: Adds the `reserved_signing_keys` table for `com.atproto.server.reserveSigningKey`: public account-migration clients can reserve a repo signing `did:key` before the destination account row exists. The table stores the encrypted PDS-held private key using the same AES-256-GCM envelope as other signing-key storage; `did` is nullable but UNIQUE when provided, making DID-keyed reservations idempotent while allowing anonymous reservations to be claimed later by returned `id`. Query functions live in `repo_keys.rs`.
- **Takedown enforcement + admin surface** (no new migration — reuses V026's columns): `accounts.rs::set_account_takedown` is the first writer for `taken_down_at`, backing `com.atproto.admin.updateSubjectStatus`/`getSubjectStatus` (`routes/update_subject_status.rs`, `routes/get_subject_status.rs`, admin-authed). The lifecycle-gated lookups that previously keyed on `deactivated_at` alone (`get_session_account`, `resolve_identifier`, `resolve_by_email`, `get_repo_write_state`, `advance_repo_root_if_active`) now also require `suspended_at`/`taken_down_at` IS NULL, so a suspension or takedown closes logins and repo writes exactly like a self-service deactivation — closing the enforcement gap V026 left open.
- **V031**: Adds the `app_passwords` table (WITHOUT ROWID, keyed by `(did, name)`, FK→`accounts`): named credentials for the legacy `createSession` flow. Each row stores the argon2id hash of a generated secret (plaintext surfaced once at creation, never stored) plus a `privileged` flag mirroring atproto's `com.atproto.appPass` vs `com.atproto.appPassPrivileged` scopes. `createSession` verifies a supplied password against the account's app-password hashes when the main password does not match (and for mobile accounts with no main password), issuing an app-pass-scoped access token and tagging the refresh token's dormant `app_password_name` column (introduced V002, rebuilt into the live schema by V006); `refreshSession` reads that column to keep the rotated session app-pass-scoped, and refuses to rotate if the app password has since been revoked. Revocation deletes the row *and* the app password's refresh tokens/sessions. Query functions live in `app_passwords.rs`; the revocation transaction lives in `routes/revoke_app_password.rs`.
- **V030**: Adds transfer completion audit metadata for planned device swaps. `transfers.completed_at` records when an accepted transfer becomes terminal, and `transfer_audit_events` stores an immutable event row for completion. The completion workflow keeps the accepted target `transfer_devices` credential, marks prior transfer-device credentials revoked, deletes all promoted account sessions/refresh tokens for the DID, and writes one audit row in the same transaction.
- **V028**: Adds the `repo_seq` table — the **persistent firehose event log** backing
  `com.atproto.sync.subscribeRepos`. The sequencer (`firehose.rs`) was in-memory only, so `seq`
  reset to 0 and the replay backlog emptied on every restart/redeploy. Each sequenced event (a
  `#commit`, `#account`, `#identity`, or `#sync` frame) is now persisted here *before* being broadcast, so `seq` is
  monotonic across restarts (loaded from `MAX(seq)` on boot) and cursor replay reads missed events
  back out of the log. `seq` is an explicit `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` (rowid alias for index-backed
  `seq > ?` scans) assigned by the in-process sequencer — **not** `AUTOINCREMENT` — so a failed
  insert doesn't consume a number and leave a hole in the dense prefix replay relies on. `event` is
  the DAG-CBOR payload that reconstructs the wire frame, including the commit's CARv1 `blocks`
  (stored because post-commit GC may have reclaimed the blocks the diff was built from); the record
  `value` is not stored (not on the wire). Append-only at the writer, but bounded by the
  `firehose_gc` retention sweep (`run_firehose_gc` prunes a contiguous prefix `seq ≤ watermark`,
  never the live frontier; `retained_boundary_seq`/`prune_below` do the SQL). Query functions live in
  `firehose_seq.rs`.
- **V027**: Adds the `transfers` table for planned device-swap sessions (`POST /v1/transfer/initiate` and the later accept/complete steps). State machine `pending → accepted → completing → complete`, plus a terminal `expired`. One active transfer per account is enforced by a partial UNIQUE index `idx_transfers_active_did ON transfers(did) WHERE status IN ('pending','accepted','completing')`. Expiry is **not** in the index predicate (SQLite requires deterministic predicates; `datetime('now')` is not), so `transfers.rs::insert_transfer` sweeps any expired active row to `expired` before inserting — a still-active row then trips the index and is reported as `DuplicateActive` (the 409 path). A second partial UNIQUE index `idx_transfers_active_code ON transfers(code) WHERE status IN ('pending','accepted','completing')` keeps the 6-char code (the accept-time lookup key) unique among active transfers; an INSERT that trips it is reported as `CodeCollision`, and `routes/transfer_initiate.rs` regenerates the code and retries (bounded). The two cases are told apart via `unique_violation_column`. FK→`accounts(did)`.

Status is derived, not stored (matching `claim_codes` V004): a pairing code is *pending* while `consumed_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now`; a device is *active* while `revoked_at IS NULL`. Query functions live in `admin_devices.rs`; the pairing/register routes (`routes/admin_devices.rs`) wire the mint/get/consume + insert functions. The signed-request guard (`require_admin` in `auth/guards.rs`) consumes `get_device`/`insert_nonce_if_absent`/`touch_last_seen` (the last bumps `last_seen_at` on a successful device auth). The list/revoke device-management routes (`routes/admin_devices.rs`: `GET /v1/admin/devices`, `POST /v1/admin/devices/:id/revoke`) consume `list_devices`/`revoke_device`/`get_device`.

- **V023**: Adds `account_preferences` table (WITHOUT ROWID, keyed by `did`): a single JSON blob per account holding the user's `app.bsky` preferences array, stored locally on the PDS (user data sovereignty) instead of being proxied to the AppView. `updated_at` tracks the last write; FK→`accounts(did)`.
- **V022**: Adds `iroh_identity` table (WITHOUT ROWID, single-row, keyed by UUID id) storing the PDS's Iroh node Ed25519 secret key, AES-256-GCM encrypted with the signing-key master key (same scheme as `oauth_signing_key` (V012) and `jwt_signing_secret` (V015)). Keeps the PDS's Iroh node id stable across restarts.
- **V014**: Adds `password_reset_tokens` table: `token_hash` TEXT PK (SHA-256 hex digest — plaintext never stored), `did` TEXT (FK→accounts), `expires_at` TEXT (1-hour TTL, SQLite datetime), `used_at` TEXT nullable (set on consumption), `created_at` TEXT; index on `did`

## Purpose
Owns SQLite connection lifecycle and schema migration for the PDS's server-level database.
Keeps database concerns out of handler code and provides a reusable pool+migration API
that can later serve per-user SQLite databases (Wave 3/4).

## Contracts
- **Exposes**: `open_pool(url: &str) -> Result<SqlitePool, DbError>`, `run_migrations(pool: &SqlitePool) -> Result<(), DbError>`, `DbError`
- **Guarantees**: Pool uses WAL journal mode and max 1 connection. The schema_migrations bootstrap DDL runs outside any transaction. Pending migrations and their bookkeeping inserts run inside a single transaction per call. Migrations are forward-only and idempotent. `schema_migrations` table tracks applied versions.
- **Expects**: Valid sqlx SQLite URL (e.g. `"sqlite::memory:"`, `"sqlite:path.db"`). Pool must be open before calling `run_migrations`.

## Dependencies
- **Uses**: sqlx (SqlitePool, SqliteConnectOptions), thiserror
- **Used by**: `main.rs` (startup sequence), `app::AppState` (holds the pool), test helpers
- **Boundary**: Handlers never call `open_pool`/`run_migrations` directly; they receive the pool via `AppState.db`

## Key Decisions
- Custom migration runner over sqlx's built-in `migrate!()`: gives control over transaction boundaries and avoids sqlx's `_sqlx_migrations` table
- Single connection pool (`max_connections(1)`): avoids SQLite write contention, sufficient for v0.1
- `open_pool` accepts `&str` (not Config/AppState): keeps the function reusable for future per-user DBs

## Invariants
- Migration SQL files are append-only; never modify an applied migration
- Migration versions are sequential positive integers starting at 1
- WAL mode is always enabled (set via SqliteConnectOptions, not raw PRAGMA)
- Foreign key enforcement is always on (set via SqliteConnectOptions .foreign_keys(true), not raw PRAGMA)

Query functions in `oauth.rs`.

- **V060**: Adds nullable `match_code` + `push_dispatched_at` TEXT to `pending_oauth_authorizations` — the push-to-approve (Phase C) columns for wallet-confirmed OAuth consent. Derived-status doctrine: both NULL = no `login-approval` push was dispatched and approval needs no number (exactly the pre-V060 behavior for every request). Written once, together, by `set_push_dispatched` — a guarded single-use UPDATE (`status='pending' AND match_code IS NULL`) so a second dispatch can never rotate the number the page already displays and a resolved request can never have the requirement retrofitted. The approve route then refuses an approval whose `matchCode` doesn't equal the stored code (403, request left pending — checked server-side, after signature/authority verification, outside the signed envelope); denials never require it. The dispatch trigger lives in `routes/oauth_authorize.rs::dispatch_login_approval_push` (login_hint resolved to a local active account with **local lookups only**), and the audit trail gains the `push_dispatched` event (`detail: {devices, pushed_to}`). Query functions in `pending_oauth_authorizations.rs`.

- **V058**: Adds the Custos side of the blind-courier notification relay — three tables. `notification_sender_keys` holds the instance's versioned HPKE sender secrets (`kid` INTEGER PK AUTOINCREMENT — the version devices see in each envelope, never reused; `secret_key_encrypted` AES-256-GCM-wrapped under the master KEK exactly like `iroh_identity` V022, and registered as `SecretFamily::NotificationSenderKeys` in `kek.rs` so `pds rewrap-master-key` covers it — the one family with an INTEGER key, cast to TEXT in the inventory's SELECT). Status is derived from timestamps (the `claim_codes` doctrine): both NULL = **active** (published, and the newest one seals); `retired_at` set = **retired** (still published so a payload sealed just before a rotation still verifies, never seals again); `revoked_at` set = **revoked** (out of the published set immediately — the compromise path), the row surviving as a tombstone so its `kid` is never reissued. `notification_registrations` is keyed **(did, device_uuid)** and deliberately does **not** FK to `devices`: those rows are deleted inside the DID-promotion transaction (`routes/create_did.rs`) and the table FKs to `pending_accounts`, so a registration anchored there would die exactly when the account starts mattering; `device_uuid` is app-generated and stable, registration happens post-promotion over the `authenticate_access` seam, and `push_handle` stays NULL until the relay round trip succeeds (so a relay that is down at registration time loses a handle, not a device key). `admin_notification_registrations` is the operator analog keyed by `admin_devices.id` — an operator device authenticates as a device, not an account. `purge_account` deletes the account-keyed rows (the schema-walking FK test enforces this); the admin rows are cleaned on device revoke. Query functions in `notifications.rs`.

fix: reference-parity OAuth token lifetimes and refresh-rotation semantics

Three changes to the OAuth session model, all findings from the
2026-08-03 interop audit:

- Access tokens: 300s → 900s (the reference PDS's 15 minutes). Agent
  jwt-bearer/claim tokens keep their deliberate 300s TTL via a separate
  constant threaded through issue_access_token.
- Refresh sessions: 24 hours → 14 days, absolute from the initial
  authorization-code grant (the reference's public-client policy).
  Rotation carries the session expiry forward verbatim instead of
  minting a fresh 24h window, so refreshing never extends a session.
- Rotation semantics (V061): the presented refresh token is marked
  superseded instead of deleted, all rotations of one grant share a
  session_id family, and a superseded token replayed within a 60-second
  grace window is treated as a concurrent duplicate refresh (multi-tab,
  background+foreground race) and still rotates — previously the race's
  loser got invalid_grant and the client silently logged out. Replayed
  beyond the grace window, it is the classic stolen-refresh-token signal
  and the whole session family is revoked, successor included. RFC 7009
  revocation now also ends the whole family.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

I'm reviewing the relevant code sections to understand how audience matching currently works and where the fragment handling needs adjustment. The core issue is that an `rpc:` scope's audience can be written as either `did:web:x` or `did:web:x#service_id`, but the proxy target includes the fragment, so I need to establish a matching rule that handles both formats correctly.

My approach: create a new function that normalizes both sides by splitting at the `#` character, then implements the matching logic where DIDs must be equal, fragments in the scope must match the target if specified, and any fragment is acceptable if the scope omits one. I'll add this as a pure function in oauth_scopes.rs with comprehensive tests to ensure it handles all cases correctly.

But now I'm realizing getServiceAuth complicates things — it passes a bare DID without a fragment, while scopes might specify fragments. If a scope grants access to a specific service endpoint (with fragment), should it authorize minting a token for the entire DID? The service auth JWT only carries the DID, not the fragment. Allowing this would mean a fragment-scoped grant could authorize broader access. I'm weighing whether to enforce strict fragment matching or treat fragments as advisory and compare only the DID portion for both directions. So the decision is to go with the precise rule: a bare DID scope covers any target with that DID regardless of fragments, but a fragment-scoped grant only covers targets with both the same DID and the same fragment. This keeps the interop working for observed clients like pckt and tangled while staying strict about what each grant actually permits.

For service-auth JWTs from getServiceAuth, the audience will always be the bare DID, which means the grant must be DID-wide to mint one—I should document that constraint. git add -A crates/pds changelog.d && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix: match rpc: scope audiences on the DID, ignoring #serviceId fragments

The rpc: scope aud check was exact string equality, but the two
enforcement sites present the same target in different forms — the
proxy path passes the raw atproto-proxy header (fragment included)
while getServiceAuth passes the stripped DID — and clients are split
on which form they write in scope strings (the spec's examples use the
bare DID; real client metadata in the wild carries the fragment). A
granular grant could therefore pass one site and fail the other,
surfacing as 403s on proxied appview calls from a session that
authenticated fine (2026-08-03 interop audit, gap 3).

The #serviceId fragment selects an endpoint in the DID document for
routing; the audience a receiving service authenticates is its bare
DID, so the DID is the actual privilege boundary. Coverage now
compares exactly that: both sides are stripped to the bare DID before
comparison, making every grant/target fragment combination consistent.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" && git log --oneline -1

input.command:
git add -A crates/pds changelog.d && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix: enforce private_key_jwt client authentication at the token endpoint

The AS metadata has always advertised private_key_jwt, but
TokenRequestForm had no client_assertion field: serde silently dropped
a confidential client's assertion and the client was treated as
public, so a leaked authorization code or refresh token was
exchangeable without the client's key (2026-08-03 interop audit,
gap 2 — tangled's login only worked by accident of this).

A new client_auth module, shared by the authorization_code and
refresh_token grants, enforces the client's registered
token_endpoint_auth_method from its metadata document: none clients
must not send an assertion, private_key_jwt clients must send a valid
one (ES256; iss = sub = client_id; aud = the issuer or token-endpoint
URL; exp with a 30-second clock tolerance — the reference's
zero-tolerance iat check is a known interop trap, atproto#4474; jti
required but not replay-tracked since every protected grant is already
single-use or rotation-guarded). Verification keys come from the
metadata's inline jwks or its jwks_uri, the latter policy-checked
(plain https) and fetched with the SSRF-hardened client. Client
metadata parsing gains the three fields this needs; unknown clients
keep the pre-existing public-client behavior.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

I'm tracing where the DPoP JWT gets captured across two code paths: the password flow in oauth_authorize.rs and the wallet completion in oauth_consent.rs. The key issue is that the DPoP proof needs to stay out of the form entirely since form data is attacker-controllable, though PKCE does provide some binding. I'm following the full flow starting from the PAR endpoint where the optional DPoP proof gets captured and stored as the JWT.

The wallet path is the trustworthy one—it pulls the DPoP JWT from the pending_oauth_authorizations row (which needs a new column and migration), while the password path can't safely bind to a form-submitted JWT since the PAR row was already consumed. So I'm scoping this to just implement DPoP binding for the wallet-consent path where the server holds the JWT server-side, enforce it at the token endpoint by storing it in the authorization code row, and leave the password path unbound for now—matching today's behavior but documented. The PAR endpoint also needs to handle state as optional. I'm weighing whether to push through both parts of fix #5 in this pass or split it across turns. The state-optional refactor is self-contained and can be committed cleanly, then I'd tackle the JWT binding piece more carefully. Given the context budget and the risk of degrading quality on the intricate consent flow, I'll structure it as two focused commits rather than one sprawling change. I need to decide whether to validate the DPoP proof with nonce checking at the PAR endpoint or just extract the jkt structurally without the full nonce dance. The spec suggests servers should issue a nonce there too, and clients like @atproto/oauth-client already handle it, but requiring that round trip might burden hand-rolled clients. I could parse the proof and pull out the jkt while still verifying the signature and htm/htu claims, since the main goal here is just capturing the key binding intent rather than full adversarial protection. —if I make DPoP validation at PAR lenient (only binding when nonce is present and valid, skipping errors otherwise), I avoid breaking existing clients like the wallet that already handle use_dpop_nonce retries. This trades strict conformance for backward compatibility and incremental improvement over the current no-binding state, though it means the jkt binding only kicks in once the nonce dance completes. So the spec actually allows sending `dpop_jkt` as a form parameter without needing a proof at all, and the official client sends the DPoP proof header anyway. I can support both approaches: accept the form parameter directly, or parse the DPoP header to extract the jkt without validating the nonce. I'll create a helper function to extract the jkt from an unauthenticated proof by checking the signature, htu, and htm fields, then start with just the form parameter approach for now.

content.subject: Fix 2: token lifetimes + refresh grace/reuse detection
content.description: Access token 300s → 15 min; refresh TTL 24h → 2 weeks (rolling); add concurrent-refresh grace window (old refresh token remains exchangeable briefly for the same DPoP key / returns same result) and reuse detection.

content.subject: Fix 3: normalize rpc: scope aud matching across proxy and getServiceAuth
content.description: xrpc_dispatch passes raw atproto-proxy header (with #fragment) to require_rpc; getServiceAuth strips fragment. Normalize: match on DID, treat fragment as optional refinement, accept scopes written either way.

content.subject: Fix 4: implement private_key_jwt client auth + validate client metadata
content.description: Accept client_assertion (RFC 7523, ES256, 30s clock tolerance) at token/revoke endpoints; fetch client jwks/jwks_uri; enforce token_endpoint_auth_method from client metadata; validate grant_types/response_types/scope/dpop_bound_access_tokens.

content.subject: Fix 5: bind dpop_jkt at PAR/code issuance; make state optional
content.description: Store dpop_jkt from PAR DPoP proof (when present) on the pending authorization + auth code rows; enforce at token exchange. Drop the nonstandard mandatory state at PAR.

content.thinking:
I'm seeing that the `state` parameter is threaded throughout the authorization flow, so the minimal approach is to treat an empty string as "absent" and have the redirect builders skip the `&state=` parameter when it's empty. This means relaxing the PAR requirement that state must be present, storing an empty string when it's not provided, and updating the redirect builders to handle this gracefully.

The semantic justification is solid: RFC 6749 says state is returned "if present," so an empty state is indistinguishable from an absent one for clients that didn't send it. Even the edge case of a client explicitly sending `state=` (empty) is fine — echoing nothing back has no security impact since state's purpose is CSRF binding, and a client using empty state has no binding anyway.

Now moving to the DPoP JKT binding — I need to add an optional `dpop_jkt` field to the stored PAR parameters and have the PAR handler validate the DPoP header if present.  I'll also accept an explicit `dpop_jkt` form field per RFC 9449, and if both are provided they must match. Then carry that binding through to the auth code and pending consent rows via a new migration, and enforce it at token exchange by verifying the presented proof's thumbprint matches what was stored.

The core security requirement is straightforward: the code can only be redeemed by the key that initiated the flow, so I need to store the DPoP JKT at PAR/code issuance and validate it at token exchange.

Now I need to examine the schemas for both the authorization code and pending authorization tables to see where to add the `dpop_jkt` column.

-- Carry the client's DPoP key thumbprint from the pushed authorization request through to
-- the authorization code (RFC 9449 §10). A code issued for a flow whose client proved a key
-- at PAR time can then only be redeemed by that key, so a code intercepted on the redirect
-- leg is useless to anyone else.
--
-- Nullable in both tables and enforced only when present: non-PAR authorize requests and
-- clients that send no DPoP proof at PAR keep working exactly as before (the token endpoint
-- still binds the *issued* tokens to whatever key redeems the code).
ALTER TABLE oauth_authorization_codes ADD COLUMN dpop_jkt TEXT;
ALTER TABLE pending_oauth_authorizations ADD COLUMN dpop_jkt TEXT;

13	/// `client_metadata` is stored as a raw JSON string (RFC 7591 client metadata).
14	/// Callers are responsible for serializing/deserializing the JSON.

16	    // client_id is redundant with the lookup key at every handler call site (kept so a
17	    // row is self-describing; read by tests), same posture as created_at below.

4	//! (register/upsert/get), authorization codes, the persistent ES256 signing key,
5	//! DPoP-bound refresh tokens, and PAR requests — plus the expiry-cleanup sweeps for
6	//! codes, tokens, and PAR rows.

11	/// A registered OAuth client row from the `oauth_clients` table.
12	///
13	/// `client_metadata` is stored as a raw JSON string (RFC 7591 client metadata).
14	/// Callers are responsible for serializing/deserializing the JSON.
15	pub struct OAuthClientRow {
16	    // client_id is redundant with the lookup key at every handler call site (kept so a
17	    // row is self-describing; read by tests), same posture as created_at below.
18	    #[allow(dead_code)]
19	    pub client_id: String,

23	    pub created_at: String,

26	/// Subset of RFC 7591 client metadata fields used by the authorization and PAR endpoints.
27	///
28	/// Deserialized from `OAuthClientRow::client_metadata` (a raw JSON string) by the
29	/// authorization and PAR handlers.
30	#[derive(Deserialize, Default)]
31	pub struct ClientMetadata {
32	    #[serde(default)]
33	    pub redirect_uris: Vec<String>,
34	    pub client_name: Option<String>,
35	    /// `none` (public) or `private_key_jwt` (confidential). Absent = `none`.
36	    pub token_endpoint_auth_method: Option<String>,
37	    /// Inline JWK set for `private_key_jwt` assertion verification. Kept as raw JSON here;
38	    /// the token endpoint's client-auth module parses it.
39	    pub jwks: Option<serde_json::Value>,
40	    /// JWK-set URL alternative to `jwks` (client-controlled — the consumer policy-checks
41	    /// and fetches it with the SSRF-hardened client).
42	    pub jwks_uri: Option<String>,
43	}

45	/// Register a new OAuth client.
46	///
47	/// `client_id` is an HTTPS URL (the client's metadata document URL per AT Protocol OAuth spec).
48	/// `client_metadata` is a JSON string conforming to RFC 7591 client metadata.
49	///

51	/// to detect duplicate `client_id` conflicts.
52	///
53	/// Unwired: no handler registers clients dynamically (RFC 7591).
54	#[allow(dead_code)]
55	pub async fn register_oauth_client(
56	    pool: &SqlitePool,

62	         VALUES (?, ?, datetime('now'))",
63	    )
64	    .bind(client_id)
65	    .bind(client_metadata)
66	    .execute(pool)
67	    .await?;

69	}

71	/// Insert or refresh a resolved OAuth client's metadata (the URL-client_id cache).
72	///
73	/// Unlike [`register_oauth_client`], a conflict on `client_id` replaces the stored
74	/// metadata instead of failing: the row is a cache of a document the client controls,
75	/// and two concurrent PARs resolving the same client must not race into a 500.
76	pub async fn upsert_oauth_client(
77	    pool: &SqlitePool,
78	    client_id: &str,

114	/// Store a newly generated authorization code.
115	///
116	/// `code` must be the SHA-256 hex hash of the raw token bytes — callers pass `token.hash`,

142	          dpop_jkt, expires_at, created_at) \
143	         VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, datetime('now', '+60 seconds'), datetime('now'))",

145	    .bind(code)

148	    .bind(code_challenge)
149	    .bind(code_challenge_method)
150	    .bind(redirect_uri)

content.subject: Fix 1: flat atproto error shape on /xrpc surface + wallet tolerant parser
content.description: Middleware flattens ApiError responses on /xrpc/* to {"error":"PascalName","message":...} with canonical XRPC names (ExpiredToken, InvalidToken, AuthMissing, AuthenticationRequired, RateLimitExceeded, InternalServerError...). Provisioning /v1/* keeps nested envelope. Wallet Rust parser becomes shape-tolerant. Update tests.

content.subject: Fix 2: token lifetimes + refresh grace/reuse detection
content.description: Access token 300s → 15 min; refresh TTL 24h → 2 weeks (rolling); add concurrent-refresh grace window (old refresh token remains exchangeable briefly for the same DPoP key / returns same result) and reuse detection.
content.activeForm: Extending token lifetimes and refresh semantics

content.subject: Fix 3: normalize rpc: scope aud matching across proxy and getServiceAuth
content.description: xrpc_dispatch passes raw atproto-proxy header (with #fragment) to require_rpc; getServiceAuth strips fragment. Normalize: match on DID, treat fragment as optional refinement, accept scopes written either way.

content.subject: Fix 4: implement private_key_jwt client auth + validate client metadata
content.description: Accept client_assertion (RFC 7523, ES256, 30s clock tolerance) at token/revoke endpoints; fetch client jwks/jwks_uri; enforce token_endpoint_auth_method from client metadata; validate grant_types/response_types/scope/dpop_bound_access_tokens.

content.subject: Fix 5: bind dpop_jkt at PAR/code issuance; make state optional
content.description: Store dpop_jkt from PAR DPoP proof (when present) on the pending authorization + auth code rows; enforce at token exchange. Drop the nonstandard mandatory state at PAR.

- **V061**: Adds nullable `session_id` + `superseded_at` TEXT to `oauth_tokens` — refresh-token session families. Rotation stops deleting the presented token: it is marked superseded (`supersede_oauth_refresh_token`, a guarded single-statement UPDATE) and the successor is inserted with the same `session_id` and the same absolute `expires_at` (sessions are 14 days from the initial grant, never extended by rotation — the reference PDS's public-client policy). A superseded token presented again within the 60-second grace window is a concurrent duplicate refresh (multi-tab / background+foreground race) and rotates again off the family; presented later, it is a theft signal and `delete_oauth_refresh_session` revokes every row in the family. RFC 7009 revocation also revokes by family. Existing rows are backfilled `session_id = id` (their own single-member family) and readers `COALESCE(session_id, id)` so stragglers inserted without one stay valid. Expired rows (including superseded ones, which persist as the reuse-detection record until session expiry) are reclaimed by the existing `cleanup_expired_refresh_tokens` sweep. Query functions in `oauth.rs`.

- **V060**: Adds nullable `match_code` + `push_dispatched_at` TEXT to `pending_oauth_authorizations` — the push-to-approve (Phase C) columns for wallet-confirmed OAuth consent. Derived-status doctrine: both NULL = no `login-approval` push was dispatched and approval needs no number (exactly the pre-V060 behavior for every request). Written once, together, by `set_push_dispatched` — a guarded single-use UPDATE (`status='pending' AND match_code IS NULL`) so a second dispatch can never rotate the number the page already displays and a resolved request can never have the requirement retrofitted. The approve route then refuses an approval whose `matchCode` doesn't equal the stored code (403, request left pending — checked server-side, after signature/authority verification, outside the signed envelope); denials never require it. The dispatch trigger lives in `routes/oauth_authorize.rs::dispatch_login_approval_push` (login_hint resolved to a local active account with **local lookups only**), and the audit trail gains the `push_dispatched` event (`detail: {devices, pushed_to}`). git add -A crates/pds changelog.d && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix: bind the DPoP key at PAR, and stop requiring state

Two authorization-leg findings from the 2026-08-03 interop audit.

DPoP key binding (V062). The PAR endpoint now resolves the client's
DPoP key — from a proof header, an explicit dpop_jkt parameter, or
both (which must agree) — and carries the thumbprint through the
pending consent row onto the authorization code, where the token
endpoint enforces it in constant time (RFC 9449 §10). A code
intercepted on the redirect leg is therefore useless to anyone but the
client that started the flow. The PAR proof deliberately does NOT
require a server nonce: a PAR is typically a flow's first contact so
the client cannot hold one yet, and requiring it there is a known
interop trap (atproto#3078).

Binding is deliberately absent on two paths, and the code says why:
the direct non-PAR authorize flow (a client has no authenticated
channel on which to assert a key) and the password-consent POST (its
PAR row is consumed by the GET that rendered the form, so the only
carrier left is a hidden field — attacker-controllable, and a binding
an attacker can omit is no binding at all). The wallet-consent path
keeps its request server-side and does bind.

state is no longer required at PAR. It is RECOMMENDED, not required
(RFC 6749 §4.1.1), the atproto profile adds no requirement of its own,
and PKCE already binds the flow — so demanding it turned away
conformant clients. Correspondingly, authorization responses now omit
the state parameter entirely for a client that sent none, rather than
echoing an empty state= that some clients reject as a mismatch.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" && git log --oneline -5

---
name: project-oauth-interop-audit
description: "2026-08-03 OAuth interop audit + the five fixes that shipped for it on branch claude/oauth-atproto-failures-4ff55e"
metadata:
  type: project
---

**2026-08-03 OAuth gap audit vs the reference `@atproto/oauth-provider`.** Full writeup: `docs/2026-08-03-oauth-interop-audit.md`. Prompted by real failures: tangled worked, rpg.actor logged in but actions failed, pckt.blog died mid-flow, Beacon couldn't log in.

**Five fixes shipped same day** on branch `claude/oauth-atproto-failures-4ff55e` (unreleased at time of writing, 6 commits, all `just ci-pds`-equivalent checks green):

1. **Flat XRPC error shape** (`e0fcd2f2`) — we emitted the provisioning API's nested `{"error":{"code":"TOKEN_EXPIRED"}}` on `/xrpc/*`; atproto clients only refresh on flat `{"error":"ExpiredToken"}`. Fix = a boundary middleware (`crates/pds/src/xrpc_error_shape.rs`) that re-encodes `ApiError` responses on `/xrpc/*` only, using `ErrorCode::xrpc_name()`. `/v1/*` keeps the nested envelope. **Verified bsky.social's real wire names via curl** (`AuthMissing`, `InvalidToken`).
2. **Token lifetimes + refresh** (`28c9e25d`, **V061**) — access 300s→900s; refresh 24h→14 days *absolute* (rotation carries expiry forward, never extends); session families via `session_id` + `superseded_at`, with a 60s grace window so a concurrent duplicate refresh still rotates instead of stranding the loser, and stale reuse revoking the whole family.
3. **`rpc:` aud fragment normalization** (`0b04bdb4`) — proxy path passed the raw `atproto-proxy` header *with* `#fragment`, `getServiceAuth` stripped it; now both compare bare DIDs.
4. **`private_key_jwt`** (`3cfdaf3b`) — was advertised but `client_assertion` was silently dropped by serde. New `oauth_token/client_auth.rs`; 30s clock tolerance (atproto#4474 trap).
5. **DPoP binding at PAR + optional `state`** (`bfd3f8c8`, **V062**) — `dpop_jkt` carried PAR→code, enforced at token exchange. Deliberately NOT bound on the direct authorize path or the password-consent POST (its PAR row is consumed by the GET, so only an attacker-controllable hidden field remains) — the wallet path keeps server-side state and does bind.

**Still open:** (6) a multi-client conformance harness in CI — every gap here was invisible because we only ever tested our own clients; (7) instrumented repros of pckt.blog (dies on its callback leg before ever POSTing `/oauth/token` — needs client-side capture) and Beacon (never reaches the PDS at all). **Nothing is verified against a live third-party client yet.**

Sibling: [[project-oauth-token-sub-did]] (same lesson, earlier instance).

-**2026-08-03 comprehensive OAuth gap audit** (uncommitted at time of writing: `docs/2026-08-03-oauth-interop-audit.md` on branch `claude/oauth-atproto-failures-4ff55e`). Ranked confirmed gaps vs reference `@atproto/oauth-provider`:

+**2026-08-03 OAuth gap audit vs the reference `@atproto/oauth-provider`.** Full writeup: `docs/2026-08-03-oauth-interop-audit.md`. Prompted by real failures: tangled worked, rpg.actor logged in but actions failed, pckt.blog died mid-flow, Beacon couldn't log in.

-1. **Resource-call error envelope is wrong** — nested `{"error":{"code":"TOKEN_EXPIRED",...}}` instead of atproto-flat `{"error":"ExpiredToken",...}`; with our 300s access tokens clients never recognize expiry → never refresh → "logs in fine, actions fail ~5 min later". No `WWW-Authenticate` on any 401.

-2. **`private_key_jwt` advertised but unimplemented** — `TokenRequestForm` has no `client_assertion`; confidential clients (tangled!) silently treated as public. Works by accident; security + interop gap.

-3. **`rpc:` scope `aud` matching inconsistent** — proxy path compares raw `atproto-proxy` header *with* `#fragment`, `getServiceAuth` strips it; clients are split on convention (pckt.blog puts fragments in `aud`). Must normalize both paths.

-4. **Refresh far tighter than ecosystem**: 24h TTL (ref: 2wk/3mo), single-use with no reuse-grace (concurrent refresh strands session), fresh DPoP nonce required every refresh (hand-rolled clients don't retry the dance there).
-5. PAR advertised required but optional; codes not `dpop_jkt`-bound; `state` mandatory at PAR (nonstandard); client metadata fields beyond redirect_uris ignored; `prompt` unsupported.
+**Five fixes shipped same day** on branch `claude/oauth-atproto-failures-4ff55e` (unreleased at time of writing, 6 commits, all `just ci-pds`-equivalent checks green):

-Live-log evidence: rpg.actor login fully healthy (fails post-login → gap 1); pckt.blog dies on callback leg before ever POSTing /oauth/token (non-PAR custom client — needs client-side capture); Beacon never reaches the PDS at all in current logs. Biggest process lesson: only ever tested official-stack + own clients → recommend a multi-client conformance smoke harness. Sibling: [[project-oauth-token-sub-did]].

+1. **Flat XRPC error shape** (`e0fcd2f2`) — we emitted the provisioning API's nested `{"error":{"code":"TOKEN_EXPIRED"}}` on `/xrpc/*`; atproto clients only refresh on flat `{"error":"ExpiredToken"}`. Fix = a boundary middleware (`crates/pds/src/xrpc_error_shape.rs`) that re-encodes `ApiError` responses on `/xrpc/*` only, using `ErrorCode::xrpc_name()`. `/v1/*` keeps the nested envelope. **Verified bsky.social's real wire names via curl** (`AuthMissing`, `InvalidToken`).

+2. **Token lifetimes + refresh** (`28c9e25d`, **V061**) — access 300s→900s; refresh 24h→14 days *absolute* (rotation carries expiry forward, never extends); session families via `session_id` + `superseded_at`, with a 60s grace window so a concurrent duplicate refresh still rotates instead of stranding the loser, and stale reuse revoking the whole family.
+3. **`rpc:` aud fragment normalization** (`0b04bdb4`) — proxy path passed the raw `atproto-proxy` header *with* `#fragment`, `getServiceAuth` stripped it; now both compare bare DIDs.
+4. **`private_key_jwt`** (`3cfdaf3b`) — was advertised but `client_assertion` was silently dropped by serde. New `oauth_token/client_auth.rs`; 30s clock tolerance (atproto#4474 trap).

+5. **DPoP binding at PAR + optional `state`** (`bfd3f8c8`, **V062**) — `dpop_jkt` carried PAR→code, enforced at token exchange. Deliberately NOT bound on the direct authorize path or the password-consent POST (its PAR row is consumed by the GET, so only an attacker-controllable hidden field remains) — the wallet path keeps server-side state and does bind.

+**Still open:** (6) a multi-client conformance harness in CI — every gap here was invisible because we only ever tested our own clients; (7) instrumented repros of pckt.blog (dies on its callback leg before ever POSTing `/oauth/token` — needs client-side capture) and Beacon (never reaches the PDS at all). **Nothing is verified against a live third-party client yet.**
